subject: history
title: Stone Age to Iron Age
description: Changes in Britain from the Stone Age to the Iron Age: hunter-gatherers and early farmers, Bronze Age technology and monuments, and Iron Age hill forts and tribes.

objectives.statement: Understand the change from late Neolithic hunter-gatherers to early farmers, for example Skara Brae.
Describe Bronze Age religion, technology and travel, for example Stonehenge and the use of metal.
Describe Iron Age hill forts, tribal kingdoms, farming, art and culture.
Understand how we find out about prehistory from archaeology and artefacts, and place the periods on a timeline.

items.prompt: In the early Stone Age, people moved around to find food. What do we call people who hunt animals and gather plants?
What were most Stone Age tools and weapons made from?
Skara Brae in Scotland is a famous example of what?

items.statement: Towards the end of the Stone Age, people began to farm and settle in one place.

items.prompt: Give one big change that happened when Stone Age people started farming instead of only hunting.
items.answer: They settled in one place, built homes, and grew crops and kept animals
acceptableAnswers: they grew crops and kept animals

items.statement: Stone Age people used metal tools like iron swords.

items.prompt: The Bronze Age is named after a metal. What metal is bronze mostly made from mixing?
Which famous monument on Salisbury Plain was completed during the Bronze Age?

items.statement: Bronze is harder and longer-lasting than tools made only of stone.

items.prompt: Why was learning to make bronze such an important change?
options: it could be made into stronger tools and weapons than stone
it was used to make paper
it made people move around more
it was used only for decoration

items.statement: People believe Stonehenge may have been used for ceremonies and to track the seasons.

items.prompt: The Iron Age is named after which metal that people learned to use for tools?
What was an Iron Age hill fort?
options: a settlement on a hill defended by banks and ditches
a stone castle with a moat
a small farm in a valley

items.statement: In the Iron Age, Britain was divided into areas ruled by different tribes.

items.prompt: Why did Iron Age people build hill forts?
options: to protect their people and animals from attack

items.statement: Iron Age people were skilled at metalwork and made decorated jewellery and art.

items.prompt: Which order are these periods in, from earliest to latest?
options: Stone Age → Bronze Age → Iron Age
Iron Age → Bronze Age → Stone Age
Bronze Age → Stone Age → Iron Age

items.prompt: What do we call the study of the past by digging up and examining objects people left behind?
What is the word for an object made by people in the past, such as a tool or pot, that we can study today?

items.statement: We call the time before written records 'prehistory'.
Because there are no written records from the Stone Age, we learn about it mainly from objects found in the ground.
